'''Shakib Al Hasan''' (born Khondaker Sakib Al-Hassan;<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2023-03-19 |title=Shakib graduates from AIUB; terms it 'dream come true' moment |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/sports/cricket/shakib-graduates-aiub-terms-it-dream-come-true-moment-601930 |access-date=2023-03-20 |website=The Business Standard |language=en}}</ref> [[Bengali language|Bengali]]: 
খন্দকার সাকিব আল হাসান; born 24 March, 1987) is a [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladeshi]] [[cricketer]] and current captain of the [[Bangladesh national cricket team]] in Tests and [[Twenty20 International|T20Is]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICC Men's T20 World Cup Cricket Team Records & Stats {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=89&type=trophy |access-date=2022-11-07 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref> According to [[International Cricket Council]], he is currently ranked no. 1 [[all-rounder]] in ODI and T20I cricket<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICC Men's ODI Player Rankings {{!}} ICC |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/rankings/mens/player-rankings/odi |access-date=2022-03-27 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}</ref> and is widely considered to be one of the greatest [[all-rounder]]s of all time.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Why Shakib Al Hasan is one of cricket's greatest allrounders|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/stats-analysis-why-shakib-al-hasan-is-one-of-cricket-s-greatest-allrounders-1219732|date=24 March 2020|access-date=2021-03-23|website=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Is Shakib Al Hasan a greater allrounder than Garry Sobers?|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/anantha-narayanan-is-shakib-al-hasan-a-greater-allrounder-than-garry-sobers-1257937|access-date=2021-04-25|website=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Express|first=The Financial|title=Where does Shakib stand among the greatest test all-rounders?|url=https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/sports/where-does-shakib-stand-among-the-greatest-test-all-rounders-1640519263|access-date=2021-12-29|website=The Financial Express|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-08-14 |title=The Current All-Format World XI, As Based On The ICC Rankings |url=https://wisden.com/stories/the-current-all-format-world-xi-as-based-on-the-icc-rankings |access-date=2022-03-30 |website=Wisden |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="dailycricket.com.bd">{{Cite web |title=Top Five Shakib Al Hasan Match Winning Performances |url=https://dailycricket.com.bd/en/news/top-five-shakib-al-hasan-match-winning-performances |access-date=2022-10-28 |website=dailycricket.com.bd |language=en-US}}</ref> He is known for his aggressive left-handed batting style in the [[Batting order (cricket)|middle order]] and controlled [[Left-arm orthodox spin|slow left-arm orthodox]] bowling.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> He was ranked the 90th most famous athlete in the world by [[ESPN.com|ESPN]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 World Fame 100: Who are the biggest names in sports? |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/id/26113613/espn-world-fame-100-2019 |access-date=2022-03-30 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> As of 2023, he has taken the most wickets at [[ICC Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cups]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICC Men's T20 World Cup Cricket Team Records & Stats {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=89&type=trophy |access-date=2023-04-17 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Most wickets taken in Cricket T20 World Cups 2022 |url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/1011496/cricket-t20-world-cup-wickets/ |access-date=2023-04-17 |website=Statista |language=en}}</ref>

Shakib Al Hasan made his test debut in 2007 against [[India national cricket team|India]]. His breakthrough came in the Test against [[New Zealand]] in [[Chittagong]] in 2008 where he picked up 7/36, which at the time was the best figure by a Bangladeshi bowler. In the [[2012 Asia Cup]], Shakib scored 237 runs, including three fifties, and took six wickets. Bangladesh progressed to the tournament's final for the first time, losing to Pakistan by 2 runs. Shakib Al Hasan was praised for his performance and impact in that game. His performance in [[2019 Cricket World Cup]] was widely praised by the fans and the experts. He is considered as one of the most impactful players in the [[ICC Cricket World Cup 2019|2019 ICC Cricket World Cup]], where he was the third highest run-scorer with scoring 606 runs in total.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ICC Cricket World Cup, 2019 Cricket Team Records & Stats {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=12357&type=tournament |access-date=2022-10-28 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref>

He has received 31 man-of-the-match awards and 16 man-of-the-series awards in all formats.<ref name=":9" /> Currently, he holds the third most Player of the tournament awards in all forms after [[Sachin Tendulkar]] and [[Virat Kohli]].<ref name=":10" /> Between 2009 and 2022, he captained the Bangladesh cricket team in 85 matches across all three formats.

He has been a consistent performer for his country over the years.<ref name="dailycricket.com.bd"/> Shakib is the most controversial figure in Bangladesh's cricket history, always making at to the top of the headlines.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=2022-01-11 |title=Shakib Al Hasan Disciplinary Issues: Ten Times When Bangladesh Superstar Got Involved In Controversies |url=https://www.outlookindia.com/website/story/sports-news-shakib-al-hasan-disciplinary-issues-ten-times-when-bangladesh-superstar-got-involved-in-controversies/385047 |access-date=2022-10-07 |magazine=Outlook |language=en}}</ref> He is the most followed person on [[Facebook]], [[Twitter]], and other social media platforms in Bangladesh, with more than 20 million followers. He has opened his own cricket academy in [[Dhaka]] called the "Masco Sakib Cricket Academy" in 2021. As of April 2023, Shakib holds the record for the most men's Twenty20 International wickets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Records {{!}} Twenty20 Internationals {{!}} Bowling records {{!}} Most wickets in career {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/283194.html |access-date=2022-10-28 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref>

== Early years and youth cricket ==
Born in [[Magura District|Magura]], [[Khulna Division|Khulna]], Shakib started playing cricket at an early age. According to ''[[Prothom Alo]]'' sports editor Utpal Shuvro, Shakib "was fairly proficient at cricket and was often hired to play for different villages and teams".<ref name="From Magura to No. 1">{{citation |last=Shuvro |first=Utpal |title=From Magura to No. 1 |date=6 February 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/from-magura-to-no-1-389383 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=31 October 2010}}</ref><ref name="No.1">{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-up-close-614133|title=Shakib up close |work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|date=13 January 2018|access-date=22 January 2021}}</ref> In one of those matches Shakib batted aggressively and bowled fast, as he usually did, but also chose to experiment with spin bowling which proved to be not so effective. He was picked to play for Islampur and took a wicket with his first ball; it was his first delivery with a proper cricket ball, having previously played with a [[tape ball|taped tennis ball]].<ref name="From Magura to No. 1" /><ref name="No.1"/> He spent six months training at [[Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protishtan]],<ref name="From Magura to No. 1" /><ref name="No.1"/> a government-run sports institute.<ref>The Current All-Format World XI, As Based On The ICC Rankings (wisden.com)</ref>

Shakib played his debut Under-17 match against [[United Arab Emirates national cricket team|UAE Under-17s]] in 2003 in the ACC Under-17 Cup where he got a bowling figure of 3–18 in 8 overs (with 2 maiden overs).<ref name=":3">{{cite web|url=http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/101/101668.html|title=Bangladesh Under-17s v United Arab Emirates Under-17s; Asian Cricket Council Under-17 Cup 2003/04 (Stage 2 Group B)|work=[[Cricket Archive]]|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003182044/http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/101/101668.html|archive-date=3 October 2015|access-date=9 June 2021}}</ref>

In May 2004, at the age of 17, Shakib made his first-class debut for [[Khulna Division|Khulna]] where he got a bowling figure of 0/116 of 30 overs in the 1st innings and 3/92 of 28 overs in the 2nd innings. He also scored 13 of 11 with three 4s in the 1st innings and 16 of 43 in the 2nd innings. His 1st first-class wicket was [[Rakibul Hasan]].<ref name=":4">{{cite web|title=Rajshahi, Apr 5 – 8 2005, Ispahani Mirzapore Tea National Cricket League|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ispahani-mirzapore-tea-national-cricket-league-2004-05-411038/rajshahi-division-vs-khulna-division-411062/full-scorecard|access-date=20 May 2021|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]}}</ref>

Shakib first represented Bangladesh at the Under-19 level in November 2005 in the 2005 Afro-Asia Under-19 Cup against [[India Under-19 cricket team|India Under-19]]. In his debut he scored 24 of 23 balls with four 4s and also achieving a bowling figure of 2/26 in 10 overs with 2 maidens by taking his first wicket of [[Tanmay Srivastava]].<ref name=":5">{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/afro-asia-cup-under-19s-2005-06-223558/india-under-19s-vs-bangladesh-under-19s-328173/full-scorecard|title=Visakhapatnam, Nov 19 2005, Afro-Asia Cup Under-19s|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=21 May 2021}}</ref> In the tournament, Shakib played 5 matches scoring 138 runs at an average of 38.50 and getting 5 wickets at an average of 25.20.<ref name=":6">{{cite news |title=Records / Afro-Asia Cup Under-19S, 2005/06 – Bangladesh Under-19S / Batting and Bowling Averages |work=[[ESPNcricinfo]] On 1 January 2005, Shakib made his first class debut in the match between Bangladesh Cricket Board President's XI and Zimbabweans where he scored 14 of 14 in the 1st innings and 15 of 66 in the 2nd innings. He also got bowling figure of 0/133 in 32 overs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/81/81320.html|title=Bangladesh Cricket Board President's XI v Zimbabweans|work=Cricket Archive|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421041850/https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/81/81320.html|archive-date=21 April 2021|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> In February 2005, Shakib got his 1st first-class international wicket by dismissing [[Vusimuzi Sibanda]] and five-wicket haul playing against Zimbabwe A.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/81/81672.html|title=Bangladesh A in Zimbabwe 2004/05|work=Cricket Archive|url-access=subscription|archive-date=5 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150405005921/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/81/81672.html|access-date=21 May 2021}}</ref>

== Domestic and T20 franchise cricket ==
=== National Cricket League(NCL) ===
Since 2004, Shakib has played for [[Khulna Division|Khulna]] in the [[National Cricket League]].

In 2004–05 season of the tournament, Shakib, since his debut in May 2004 at the age of 17, played just 3 matches{{efn|against [[Rajshahi Division cricket team|Rajshahi]](13 & 16,0–116 & 3–92),[[Sylhet Division cricket team|Sylhet]](12 &12,6–75 & 3–49) and [[Dhaka Division cricket team|Dhaka]]}}. He scored 129 runs at an average of 25.80 with a high score of 54 and took 16 wickets at an average of 27.87 with a best bowling figure of 6/79 in an innings and 9/114 in a match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=5145;team=751;type=tournament|title=Records / Ispahani Mirzapore Tea National Cricket League, 2004/05 – Khulna Division / Batting and Bowling Averages|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=18 June 2021}}</ref>

In the 2006–07 season, he played just 2{{efn|against [[Rajshahi Division cricket team|Rajshahi]](13 & 16,0–116 & 3–92),[[Sylhet Division cricket team|Sylhet]](12 &12,6–75 & 3–49) and [[Dhaka Division cricket team|Dhaka]]}} matches scoring 51 runs at an average 17.00 with a high score of 23. He bowled only in 1 innings where he bowled 4 overs of 9 runs with 1 maiden over without any wicket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/champions-league-twenty014/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=2974;team=751;type=tournament|title=ISPAHANI MIRZAPORE TEA NATIONAL CRICKET LEAGUE, 2006/07 - KHULNA DIVISION / RECORDS / BATTING AND BOWLING AVERAGES|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=24 December 2021}}</ref>

Shakib has played 14 matches scoring 933 runs at an average of 40.43 with three 100s and a high score of 129.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/f_Batting_by_Team.html|title=First-Class Batting and Fielding for Each Team by Shakib Al Hasan|work=Cricket Archive|archive-date=21 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521060029/https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/f_Batting_by_Team.html|access-date=21 May 2021}}</ref> He also got 31 wickets at an average of 33.16 with 1 5-wicket haul.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/f_Bowling_by_Team.html|title=FIRST-CLASS BOWLING FOR EACH TEAM BY SHAKIB AL HASAN|work=Cricket Archive|archive-date=21 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521062335/https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/f_Bowling_by_Team.html|access-date=21 May 2021}}</ref>

=== English County Cricket(ECC) ===
==== County Championship ====
Having signed a contract in November 2009,<ref name="Shakib for Worcestershire">{{citation |url=http://www.worcesternews.co.uk/sport/wccc/4744603.Worcestershire_in_swoop_for_Shakib_as_overseas_player/ |title=Worcestershire in swoop for Shakib as overseas player |work=Worcester News |publisher=[[Newsquest]] Media Group |last=Reeves |first=Michael |date=18 November 2009 |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib joined up with [[Worcestershire County Cricket Club|Worcestershire]], playing the second division of the [[County Championship]], in July 2010. He was the first Bangladeshi to represent a county side.<ref name="Shakib for Worcestershire" /> Shakib was forced to delay by the [[Bangladesh Cricket Board|BCB]] for the beginning of his spell as Worcestershire's overseas player.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/jul/13/bangladesh-worcestershire-shakib-al-hasan|title=Bangladesh make Worcestershire wait for Shakib Al Hasan|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=15 July 2010|access-date=19 May 2021}}</ref> While playing for Worcestershire, he took his best first-class bowling figures of 7/32 against [[Middlesex County Cricket Club|Middlesex]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/live-scores/cricket/middlesex-v-worcestershire/11025|title=Shakib spins out Middlesex|work=[[Sky Sports]]|date=10 September 2010|access-date=29 March 2021}}</ref> In eight first-class matches he scored 358 runs at 25.57 (with one score over 50)<ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/f_Batting_by_Team.html|title=First-class batting and fielding for each team by Shakib Al Hasan|work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> and took 35 wickets at 22.37,<ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/f_Bowling_by_Team.html |title=First-class bowling for each team by Shakib Al Hasan |work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> as Worcestershire secured promotion to the first division at the end of the season.<ref>{{citation |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/cricket/counties/9006380.stm |title=Worcestershire win promotion with victory over Sussex |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=16 September 2010 |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref>

After the [[2011 Indian Premier League|2011 IPL]], Shakib returned to Worcestershire for seven weeks. He played a single County Championship match as his time with the team coincided with the [[2011 Friends Life t20]],<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib rejoins Worcestershire for 2011 |date=6 January 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/county-news-shakib-al-hasan-rejoins-worcestershire-for-2011-498143 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=8 January 2011}}</ref><ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/First-Class_Matches.html |title=First-class matches played by Shakib Al Hasan |work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=23 July 2011}}</ref> but in that match, he took seven wickets and passed 3,000 runs in first-class cricket.<ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/316/316169.html |title=f53262 Worcestershire v Hampshire: LV County Championship 2011 (Division 1) |work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=23 July 2011}}</ref>

Shakib played five List-A matches for Worcestershire, scoring 187 at an average of 37.40 (including two half-centuries)<ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/a_Batting_by_Team.html |title=ListA batting and fielding for each team by Shakib Al Hasan |work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=11 November 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210620162616/https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/a_Batting_by_Team.html|archive-date=20 June 2021}}</ref> and taking 9 wickets at 17.77.<ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/73/73152/a_Bowling_by_Team.html |title=ListA bowling for each team by Shakib Al Hasan |work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref>

==== Friends Life t20 ====
Worcestershire finished fifth out of nine teams in their group for the T20 competition, failing to qualify for the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/friends-life-t20-2011-491208/points-table-standings |title=Friends Life t20 2011-Table |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=23 July 2011}}</ref> From 12 matches Shakib took 19 wickets, finishing as the club's leading wicket-taker, equal with seam bowler [[Gareth Andrew]].<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=6381;type=tournament |title=Records / Friends Life t20, 2011 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=23 July 2011}}</ref> He also scored 110 runs at an average of 9.16.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/friends-life-t20/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=6381;team=1509;type=tournament|title=Friends Life T20, 2011 – Worcestershire / Records / Batting and Bowling Averages|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref>

Shakib signed for [[Leicestershire County Cricket Club|Leicestershire]] as their second overseas club, joining Australian [[Joe Burns (cricketer)|Joe Burns]] for their [[2013 Friends Life t20|Twenty 20]] campaign.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/cricket/21975899 | title=Shakib Al Hasan joins for FL t20 | date=29 March 2013 |work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC| access-date=28 September 2013}}</ref> Shakib played in 10 matches scoring 146 runs at an average of 18.25 with a top score of 43* in the 7 wicket win over [[Nottinghamshire Outlaws]] at [[Trent Bridge]].<ref name="Friends">{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=7907;team=1184;type=tournament|title=Records / Friends Life T20, 2013 – Leicestershire / Batting and Bowling Averages|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/friends-life-t20-2013-592761/leicestershire-vs-nottinghamshire-north-division-593642/full-scorecard|title=Result-North Division, Leicester, Jul 12 2013, Friends Life t20|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref> He also got 9 wickets at an average of 27.00 with an economy of 6.50 and a best bowling figure of 2/7 in the 10 wicket win over Yorkshire.<ref name="Friends" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leicestershireccc.co.uk/news/2020/august/south-asian-heritage-bangladesh-and-afghanistan.html|title=South Asian Heritage – Bangladesh and Afghanistan|work=[[Leicestershire County Cricket Club]] |date=6 August 2020|access-date=30 December 2020}}</ref>

=== Indian Premier League(IPL) ===
Although Shakib was part of the auction of players held the following month for the [[2009 Indian Premier League]], Shakib was not chosen by any of the eight teams and no bids were made for him despite being rated as the world's highest-ranked ODI all-rounder at the time. His teammate [[Mashrafe Mortaza]], who was bought in the auction by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]], said "I would have been a lot happier if Shakib had got a team because he truly deserved it for his sensational form with the bat and ball".<ref>{{citation |title=Proud Mortaza credits hard work |date=6 February 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/proud-mortaza-credits-hard-work-389524 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=7 February 2009}}</ref> Shakib had no buyers in the [[List of 2010 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2010 IPL auction]] as well, which was very surprising considering his stature in international cricket at the time.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2010/01/19/shakib-unsold-in-ipl-auction2|title=Shakib unsold in IPL auction|work=bdnews24.com|date=18 January 2010|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://cricket.yahoo.net/news/ipl-5-t20-legends-gone-083518152|title=IPL: 5 T20 legends who have gone unsold in an auction|work=Spoortskeeda|date=30 July 2020|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref>

For the [[2011 Indian Premier League]], Shakib was contracted by [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] for US$425,000.<ref>{{citation |title=Ryder, Kartik, Kaif go in re-bidding |date=6 January 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2011-ryder-kartik-kaif-go-in-re-bidding-495911 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=8 January 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/IPL-auction-Day-1-As-it-happened/article15513264.ece|title=IPL auction Day 1 – As it happened|work=[[The Hindu]]|date=8 January 2011|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref> He made his debut in the tournament on 15 April 2011 in a match against [[Rajasthan Royals]]. He claimed two wickets in the match, first that of [[Amit Paunikar]] and then [[Shane Watson]], but did not get the chance to bat as his team only lost a wicket, winning by 9 wickets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/indian-premier-league-2011-466304/rajasthan-royals-vs-kolkata-knight-riders-12th-match-501209/full-scorecard|title=Full Scorecard of Royals vs KKR 12th match 2011 - Score Report|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|date=15 April 2011|access-date=24 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/333/333574.html |title=tt2137 ipl188 Rajasthan Royals v Kolkata Knight Riders: Indian Premier League 2011 |work=CricketArchive |url-access=subscription |access-date=18 April 2011}}</ref> KKR were knocked out in the semi-finals of the competition;<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2011/content/story/517231.html |title=A cut above the rest |first=Nitin |last=Sundar |journal=Physics |date=30 May 2011 |volume=5 |page=139 |doi=10.1103/Physics.5.139 |bibcode=2012PhyOJ...5..139C |access-date=31 May 2011|doi-access=free }}</ref> Shakib played in seven matches, taking 11 wickets at an average of 15.90, and finished as KKR's third-highest wicket-taker.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2011/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5969;type=tournament |title=Indian Premier League, 2011 / Records / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=31 May 2011}}</ref>

In the 15th Match of the [[2012 Indian Premier League|2012 IPL]] against [[Rajasthan Royals]], Shakib got a bowling figure of 3–17 which is still his best in his [[Indian Premier League|IPL]] career.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/indian-premier-league-2012-520932/kolkata-knight-riders-vs-rajasthan-royals-15th-match-548320/match-report|title=Shakib helps Kolkata win low-scoring game|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|date=13 April 2012|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref><ref name="SAH75">{{cite web|url=https://www.iplt20.com/teams/sunrisers-hyderabad/squad/201/shakib-al-hasan|work=[[Indian Premier League]]|title=Shakib Al Hasan IPL statistics|access-date=30 December 2020}}</ref> [[Kolkata Knight Riders|KKR]] won their maiden title in the final against [[Chennai Super Kings|CSK]] where Shakib contributed with a crucial cameo.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.india.com/sports/this-is-insulting-manoj-tiwary-reacts-after-kkr-didnt-tag-him-and-shakib-al-hasan-in-ipl-2012-throwback-post-4041476/|title='This is Insulting': Manoj Tiwary Reacts After KKR Didn't Tag Him And Shakib Al Hasan in IPL 2012 Throwback Post|work=India.com|date=27 May 2020|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref>

In the [[2014 Indian Premier League]], Shakib was retained by KKR for a league fee of INR 2.80 [[crore]]. In the competition, he scored 227 runs in 11 innings at a strike rate of 149.34; his best being a 60 off 38 balls. He also achieved 11 wickets in 13 matches at an economy of 6.68 and an average of 30.36. His all-round performance was instrumental in KKR's title win. For his performances in 2014, he was named as the 12th man in the [[2014 Indian Premier League#2014 Cricinfo IPL XI|Cricinfo IPL XI]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2014-team-of-the-tournament-749617|title=The team of the tournament:ESPNcricinfo picks its team of the 2014 season, with a limit of only four foreign players in the XI |work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|date=2 June 2014|access-date=30 December 2020}}</ref>

=== Bangladesh Premier League ===

The [[Bangladesh Cricket Board]] founded the six-team [[Bangladesh Premier League]] in 2012, a twenty20 tournament to be held in February that year. The BCB made Shakib the 'icon player' for [[Khulna Royal Bengals]] (KRB).<ref>{{citation |last=Engineer |first=Tariq |title=Bangladesh Premier League to begin on February 9 |date=28 December 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-premier-league-2012-bpl-to-begin-on-february-9-next-year-547222 |publisher=[[ESPNcricinfo]] |access-date=5 March 2012}}</ref> Under his captaincy, Shakib's team progressed to the semi-finals of the competition where they were beaten by [[Dhaka Gladiators]] despite Shakib's 86[[not out|*]] off 41 balls.<ref>{{citation |title=Dhaka make final despite Shakib |date=28 February 2012 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-premier-league-2011-12-547342/dhaka-gladiators-vs-khulna-royal-bengals-2nd-semi-final-551076/match-report |publisher=[[ESPNcricinfo]] |access-date=5 March 2012}}</ref> In ten matches he scored 280 runs and took 15 wickets, which made him KRB's leading wicket-taker, and was named Man of the Tournament.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh-premier-league-2012/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=7188;type=tournament |title=Bangladesh Premier League, 2011/12 / Records / Most wickets |publisher=[[ESPNcricinfo]] |access-date=5 March 2012}}</ref><ref>{{citation |last=Isam |first=Mohammad |title=The BPL XI |date=1 March 2012 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-premier-league-2012-the-bpl-xi-555925 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=5 March 2012}}</ref>

In the [[2013 Bangladesh Premier League player auction|auction of the BPL 2]], Shakib was brought by defending champions [[Dhaka Gladiators]] for $365,000, the most expensive player in the tournament.<ref name="auto4">{{citation |last=Isam |first=Mohammad |title=Shakib the top pick at BPL auction |date=20 December 2012 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-al-hasan-the-top-pick-at-bpl-auction-597888 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=27 February 2013}}</ref> He led his team to the title, getting 329 runs and 15 wickets in 12 matches, emerging as the Man of the Tournament for the consecutive second time in the BPL.<ref name="auto2">{{citation |last=Isam |first=Mohammad |title=The BPL XI |date=20 February 2013 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/the-bpl-xi-605655 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=27 February 2013}}</ref>

=== Bangabandu T20 Cup ===

In November 2020, Shakib made a return to cricket, following the completion of a one-year ban imposed by the International Cricket Council, being selected to play for Gemcon Khulna in [[2020-21 Bangabandhu T20 Cup|Bangabandhu T20 Cup 2020]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dhakatribune.com/sport/2020/11/12/khulna-picked-shakib-for-bangabandhu-t20-cup|title=Khulna picked Shakib for Bangabandhu T20 cup|work=Dhaka Tribune|access-date=13 November 2020}}</ref>

Shakib however is the 2nd Bangladeshi batsman to score 5000 runs in T20 cricket after [[Tamim Iqbal]]. Overall he is the 65th cricketer in the world to reach the 5000 runs mark.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://dailyasianage.com/news/248368/shakib-reaches-5k-runs-achieves-rare-double-in-t20s|work=The Asian Age|location=Bangladesh|title=Shakib reaches 5K runs, achieves rare double in T20s|date=29 November 2020|access-date=22 January 2021}}</ref>

Before leaving, he made quickfire 28 and took one wicket conceding 31 runs in Khulna's crucial win against [[Gazi Group Chattogram]] in the 1st Qualifier of the tournament.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dhakatribune.com/sport/2020/12/15/shakib-to-miss-final-for-gemcon-khulna-in-bangabandhu-t20|title=Shakib to miss Bangabandu T20 final|work=[[Dhaka Tribune]]|date=15 December 2020|access-date=19 December 2020}}</ref>

Shakib played nine matches, failing to impress much by scoring only 110 runs and bagging 6 wickets.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thefinancialexpress.com.bd/sports/shakib-to-skip-bangabandhu-t20-cup-2020-final-for-family-emergency-1608020316|title=Shakib to skip 'Bangabandhu T20 Cup 2020' final for family emergency|work=[[The Financial Express (Bangladesh)|The Financial Express]]|location=Dhaka|date=15 December 2020|access-date=19 December 2020}}</ref>
