=== Debut years ===
Shakib made his [[One Day International]] (ODI) debut against [[Zimbabwe cricket team|Zimbabwe]] on 6 August 2006 at [[Harare Sports Club]]. He played a significant part in Bangladesh's victory, where he scored 30 runs and bowled out [[Elton Chigumbura]] to get his first ODI wicket.<ref name="auto3">{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/249207.html|work=ESPNcricinfo|title=Scorecard: Bangladesh tour of Zimbabwe, 5th ODI: Zimbabwe v Bangladesh at Harare, 6 August 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/98/98929.html|title=Bangladesh in Kenya and Zimbabwe 2006 (5th ODI)|work=Cricket Archive|archive-date=12 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112070926/https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/98/98929.html|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref>

On 28 November 2006, Shakib made his T20 and T20I debut against Zimbabwe. On his debut, Shakib scored 26 of 28 balls and got a bowling figure of 1/31.His 1st T20 & T20I wicket was of [[Sean Williams (cricketer)|Sean Williams]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/zimbabwe-tour-of-bangladesh-2006-07-264061/bangladesh-vs-zimbabwe-only-t20i-264065/full-scorecard|title=Only T20I, Khulna, Nov 28 2006, Zimbabwe tour of Bangladesh|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=21 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/107/107063.html|title=Zimbabwe in Bangladesh 2006/07 (Twenty20)|work=Cricket Archive|archive-date=16 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016153031/http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/107/107063.html|access-date=21 May 2021}}</ref>

Shakib made his Test debut on 6 May 2007 against [[India national cricket team|India]]. On his debut his got a bowling figure of 0/62 (19 overs) and scored 30 of 47 balls in 1st innings and 15 of 64 balls in 2nd innings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/india-tour-of-bangladesh-2007-282685/bangladesh-vs-india-2nd-test-282692/full-scorecard|title=2nd Test, Dhaka, May 25 – 27 2007, India tour of Bangladesh|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/116/116634.html|title=India in Bangladesh 2007 (1st Test) |work=Cricket Archive|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112070926/https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/116/116634.html|archive-date=12 November 2019|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> Shakib's first test wicket was [[Craig Cumming]] in [[Bangladeshi cricket team in New Zealand in 2007-08|the 2nd test vs New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-tour-of-new-zealand-2007-08-300412/new-zealand-vs-bangladesh-2nd-test-300430/full-scorecard|title=2nd Test, Wellington, Jan 12 – 14 2008, Bangladesh tour of New Zealand|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=1 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/124/124203.html|title=Bangladesh in New Zealand 2007/08 (2nd Test)|work=Cricket Archive|archive-date=1 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001051025/http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/124/124203.html|access-date= 21 May 2021}}</ref>

On 20 October 2008, Shakib took at that time the best bowling figures by a Bangladesh player in Tests, 7 wickets for 36 runs, against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] in [[New Zealand cricket team in Bangladesh in 2008-09|the 1st test of the test series]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/326173/shakib-s-all-round-show-puts-bangladesh-in-command|title=Shakib's all-round show puts Bangladesh in command|work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]|date=28 October 2008|archive-url=https://archive.today/20210520112502/https://www.dawn.com/news/326173/shakib-s-all-round-show-puts-bangladesh-in-command|archive-date=20 May 2021|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-tour-of-bangladesh-2008-09-361750/bangladesh-vs-new-zealand-1st-test-361758/full-scorecard|title=1st Test, Chattogram, Oct 17 – 21 2008, New Zealand tour of Bangladesh|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref>

From January 2009<ref>{{cite news|url=https://bdnews24.com/cricket/2009/01/22/shakib-world-s-best-odi-all-rounder|title=Shakib world's best ODI all-rounder|work=bdnews24.com|date=22 January 2009|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> to April 2011<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/icc-rankings-shane-watson-rises-top-spot-in-icc-rankings-511114|title=Watson rises to top spot in ICC rankings|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|date=15 April 2011|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> and again from March 2012<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-227859|title=Shakib regains No 1 position|work=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]]|date=27 March 2012|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> to January 2013,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/178528|title=Hafeez back as number-one ranked ODI all-rounder|work=[[International Cricket Council]]|date=1 September 2013|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/numbers-game-allrounder-hafeez-on-top-of-his-game-600403|title=Allrounder Hafeez on top of his game|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|date=11 January 2013|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> Shakib was ranked first amongst ODI all-rounders by the [[International Cricket Council|ICC]]. In December 2011, he became the world's top-ranked Test all-rounder.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://bdnews24.com/cricket/2011/12/22/shakib-best-test-allrounder|title=Shakib best Test allrounder|work=bdnews24.com|date=22 December 2011|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> In December 2014, Shakib became the world's top-ranked Twenty 20 all-rounder.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.daily-sun.com/post/19143/Shakib-Salma-ranked-No.-1-T20-allrounder|title=Shakib, Salma ranked No. 1 T-20 all-rounder|work=[[Daily Sun]]|date=7 December 2014|access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> He is currently the only all-rounder to be ranked in the top 3 of [[ICC Player Rankings]] across every format of international cricket.

Shakib was appointed Bangladesh's [[Captain (cricket)|vice-captain]] in June 2009. During Bangladesh's tour of the West Indies the following month, the captain [[Mashrafe Mortaza]] was injured and Shakib took over the captaincy. He was 22 years old at the time. Initially, a temporary position, Shakib's success against the [[West Indies]], securing his side's first overseas series win, ensured his retention of captaincy even after Mashrafe recovered. Shakib was named ''[[The Wisden Cricketer]]'s'' "Test Player of the Year" in October 2009.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-108905|title=Shakib Al Hasan, the world-beater|work=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]]|date=8 October 2009|access-date=26 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/shakib-named-wisden-test-player-of-the-year-ahead-of-gambhir-1595566|title=Shakib named Wisden Test Player of the Year ahead of Gambhir|work=[[NDTV]] SPORTS|date=8 October 2009|access-date=26 January 2021}}</ref> In July 2010, he stepped down from the ODI captaincy to concentrate on his personal performance. Mortaza took over until he became injured again and Shakib was asked to resume leadership. This lasted until he was relieved of captaincy in September 2011 due to a poor World Cup campaign.

=== Breakthrough (2006–2008) ===
Shakib was included in Bangladesh's senior squad to tour Zimbabwe in February 2006. Along with [[Farhad Reza]] and [[Mushfiqur Rahim]], Shakib was one of the three uncapped players to be included in the squad.<ref>{{citation |title=Whatmore: 'Bangladesh are favourites' |date=20 July 2006 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/whatmore-bangladesh-are-favourites-253971 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=7 November 2009}}</ref> Shakib and Reza were described as "very good cricketers in all departments of the game", and Faruq Ahmed – the chief selector – said that Bangladesh had "high hopes from them and it's time for them to perform at the international level".<ref>{{citation |title=Bangladesh name young allrounders |date=3 July 2006 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-name-young-allrounders-252258 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=7 November 2009}}</ref> Shakib made his ODI debut on the tour on 6 August; his maiden wicket was that of all-rounder [[Elton Chigumbura]], and he finished with bowling figures of 1/39. He also scored 30 not out while [[Shahriar Nafees]] scored his maiden ODI century to help Bangladesh win by eight wickets. It was the final match in the series, which Zimbabwe won 3–2.<ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/98/98929.html |title=o2398 a17537: Zimbabwe v Bangladesh, Bangladesh in Kenya and Zimbabwe 2006 (5th ODI) |work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> In September 2006, Shakib was one of three players to be granted a rookie contract with the [[Bangladesh Cricket Board]] (BCB), along with Farhad Reza and [[Mehrab Hossain, Jr.|Mehrab Hossain Jr]]. This increased the number of players with central contracts and under the control of the BCB from 20 to 23.<ref>{{citation |title=Mahmud named Bangladesh team manager |date=23 September 2006 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mahmud-named-bangladesh-team-manager-260387 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=7 November 2009}}</ref>

Shakib was included in the 15-man squad led by [[Habibul Bashar]] for  the [[2007 Cricket World Cup]] hosted  [[West Indies]] in March and April.<ref>{{citation |title=Mashud left out of Bangladesh squad |date=13 February 2007 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mashud-left-out-of-bangladesh-squad-280197 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Bangladesh made it to the second stage of the competition and finished seventh.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/wc2007/engine/series/125929.html?view=pointstable |title=ICC World Cup 2006/07 / Points table |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Along the way the team caused an upset by beating [[India national cricket team|India]] to help knock them out of the tournament. With [[Tamim Iqbal]] in just his fifth ODI and Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib was one of three Bangladesh batsmen in the match to score a half century to help the team reach its target of 192 to win.<ref>{{citation |last=Vaidyanathan |first=Siddhartha |title=Brilliant Bangladesh stun India |date=17 March 2007 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-world-cup-2006-07-125929/bangladesh-vs-india-8th-match-group-b-247464/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Later in the tournament, Shakib scored another half-century although Bangladesh were defeated by England on that very occasion.<ref>{{citation |last=Premachandran |first=Dileep |title=Saqibul stands tall but can't stop the fall |date=11 April 2008 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/saqibul-stands-tall-but-can-t-stop-the-fall-290076 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> He scored 202 runs from 9 matches at an average of 28.85 with a high score of 57[[not out|*]] and achieved 7 wickets at an average of  43.14 with an economy of 4.96.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=2403;team=25;type=tournament|title=Records / ICC World Cup, 2006/07 – Bangladesh / Batting and Bowling Averages|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=29 March 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Shakib fielding, 23 January, 2009, Dhaka SBNS.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Shakib in the 3rd and the final ODI against Zimbabwe in January 2009 in [[Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium]], which Bangladesh won with Shakib's individual unbeaten 33 runs off 60 balls<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bdeshvzim/engine/match/378759.html|title=3rd ODI: Bangladesh v Zimbabwe at Dhaka, Jan 23, 2009 – Cricket Scorecard – ESPN Cricinfo|access-date=27 October 2016}}</ref>]]
Later that year, in May, India [[Indian cricket team in Bangladesh in 2007|toured Bangladesh]] for two Tests and three ODIs. On 18 May, Shakib made his Test debut against India. He batted once, scoring 27 runs, and bowled 13 overs without taking a wicket as the match ended in a draw.<ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/116/116634.html |title=f50076 t1832: Bangladesh v India India in Bangladesh 2007 (1st Test) |work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> In his 2nd match he batted twice scoring 30 and 15 runs and bowled 19 overs without taking any wickets where also wicket-kept for 8 balls till India's innings declaration, as India won by an innings and 238 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/india-tour-of-bangladesh-2007-282685/bangladesh-vs-india-2nd-test-282692/ball-by-ball-commentary|title=RESULT 2nd Test, Dhaka, May 25 – May 27 2007, India tour of Bangladesh|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|date=27 May 2007|access-date=6 February 2021}}</ref> India won the Test series 1–0 and the ODI series 3–0. After the tour, [[Dav Whatmore]] resigned from his position as Bangladesh coach,<ref>{{citation |title=Whatmore quits as Bangladesh coach |date=20 April 2007 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/whatmore-quits-as-bangladesh-coach-291550 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> and batsman [[Mohammad Ashraful]] replaced Habibul Bashar as captain.<ref>{{citation |title=Ashraful named Bangladesh captain |date=2 June 2007 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ashraful-named-bangladesh-captain-296705 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref>

In September 2007, South Africa hosted the [[2007 ICC World Twenty20|ICC World Twenty20]]. Victory against West Indies in the first round was enough to ensure Bangladesh's progression to the second round, although it was the only one of their five matches they won. In the match against West Indies, Shakib took 4/34; it was the first time a Bangladesh player had taken more than three wickets in an International Twenty20 match (T20I).<ref>{{citation |last1=Gopalakrishna |first1=HR |title=Ashraful slams his way to fastest fifty in Bangladesh win |date=13 September 2007 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ashraful-slams-his-way-to-fastest-fifty-in-bangladesh-win-310815 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010 |last2=Varghese |first2=Mathew}}</ref> Shakib was part of another piece of T20I history when in a match against Australia in the tournament he became one of three victims of the first T20I hat-trick. [[Brett Lee]] took Shakib's wicket, followed by those of Mortaza's and [[Alok Kapali]] to help Australia to a nine-wicket win.<ref>{{citation |last=Veera |first=Sriram |title=Hayden and Lee power Australian win |date=16 September 2007 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-world-twenty20-2007-08-286109/australia-vs-bangladesh-14th-match-group-f-287866/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=26 December 2010}}</ref> In October that year, it was announced that [[Jamie Siddons]] – Australia's assistant coach – would take over the role of Bangladesh coach;<ref>{{citation |title=Siddons accepts Bangladesh job |date=28 October 2007 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/siddons-accepts-to-coach-bangladesh-317465 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Siddons asserted that the previous set-up had focused on short-term goals and that he was planning to improve Bangladesh over the long term and keep together a core squad of talented players to gain experience at international level.<ref>{{citation |title='My vision is long-term' – Siddons |date=15 January 2008 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/my-vision-is-long-term-siddons-331087 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref>

In [[Bangladeshi cricket team in New Zealand in 2007–08|December 2007 and January 2008]], Bangladesh toured New Zealand for two Tests and three ODIs. Although he did not play the first Test, Shakib was selected over [[Enamul Haque Jr]] for the second due to his better batting ability.<ref name="NZ January 2008">{{citation |last=Binoy |first=George |title=New Zealand coast to innings victory |date=14 January 2008 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-tour-of-new-zealand-2007-08-300412/new-zealand-vs-bangladesh-2nd-test-300430/match-report-2 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> It was Shakib's fourth Test, and until that point he had gone wicketless. His first wicket was that of New Zealand's [[Craig Cumming]].<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/56143.html?class=1;template=results;type=bowling;view=match |title=Statistics / Statsguru / Shakib Al Hasan / Test matches |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref><ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/124/124203.html |title=f50566 t1861: New Zealand v Bangladesh, Bangladesh in New Zealand 2007/08 (2nd Test) |work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> New Zealand won by an innings and 137 runs and took the series 2–0.<ref name="NZ January 2008" /> New Zealand also completed a clean sweep in the ODIs which preceded the Tests, winning 3–0.<ref>{{citation |last=Alter |first=Jamie |title=Vettori and McCullum thrash Bangladesh |date=30 December 2007 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/vettori-and-mccullum-thrash-bangladesh-328292 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib played in all three ODIs scoring 31 runs at an average of 10.33,<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=3308;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in New Zealand ODI Series, 2007/08 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> and taking 3 wickets at an average of 42.33.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=3308;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in New Zealand ODI Series, 2007/08 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Over [[South African cricket team in Bangladesh in 2007–08|February and March 2008 South Africa toured Bangladesh]], playing two Tests and three ODIs. South Africa won both Tests.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bdeshvrsa/engine/match/323948.html |title=South Africa in Bangladesh Test Series – 2nd Test Bangladesh v South Africa: Test no. 1865 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib played in both Bangladesh's defeats, taking just one wicket while conceding 122 runs,<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=3677;type=series |title=Records / South Africa in Bangladesh Test Series, 2007/08 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> and scoring 75 runs.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=3677;type=series |title=Records / South Africa in Bangladesh Test Series, 2007/08 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> South Africa won the subsequent ODI series 3–0.<ref>{{citation |last=Balachandran |first=Kanishkaa |title=South Africa No.1 after clean sweep |date=14 March 2008 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-tour-of-bangladesh-2007-08-323940/bangladesh-vs-south-africa-3rd-odi-323951/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib passed 1,000 ODI runs in the series; he passed the landmark in his 39th ODI with a batting average of 35.37.<ref name="ODI cumulative batting average">{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/56143.html?class=2;template=results;type=batting;view=cumulative |title=Statistics / Statsguru / Shakib Al Hasan / ODI matches cumulative batting average |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref>

Before [[New Zealand cricket team in Bangladesh in 2008–09|New Zealand's tour of Bangladesh in October 2008]], Shakib was considered more of a batsman than a bowler, despite being an all-rounder. Though he usually batted down the order at number seven in Tests, he had mostly batted in the top five in ODIs. In a departure from Shakib's usual role Jamie Siddons, the coach stated that Shakib would play the Test series against New Zealand as a specialist bowler. The move immediately paid off, and he took 7/37 in New Zealand's first innings in the opening Test which was the best bowling figures by a Bangladesh player in all their 54 Tests suppressing the previous best innings figures by a Bangladeshi bowler set by another left-armer Enamul Haque with 7–95 against Zimbabwe at Dhaka three years ago.,<ref name="From Magura to No. 1" /> He scored 71 for his maiden Test half-century to guide the home team to 184–8 in their second innings.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/326173/shakib-s-all-round-show-puts-bangladesh-in-command|title=Shakib's all-round show puts Bangladesh in command|work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]|date=20 October 2008|access-date=7 June 2021}}</ref> Bangladesh lost the series 2–0, but Shakib finished as Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker in the series with 10 wickets at 17.80.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=4494;type=series |title=Records / New Zealand in Bangladesh Test Series, 2008/09 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> His spell was nominated to be the Best Test Bowling Performance of 2008 by ESPNCricinfo.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/awards2008/content/story/385017.html|title=Test bowling: the nominees|date=2 January 2009|website=Cricinfo}}</ref>
Bangladesh won the opening match of the ODI series against New Zealand – securing their first ever ODI win over them<ref>{{citation |title=Bangladesh maul sorry New Zealand |date=9 October 2008 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-tour-of-bangladesh-2008-09-361750/bangladesh-vs-new-zealand-1st-odi-361755/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> – although they eventually lost the series 2–1.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bdeshvnz/engine/series/361750.html |title=New Zealand tour of Bangladesh 2008/09 / Results |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib finished with five wickets from three matches, making him Bangladesh's second-highest wicket-taker for the series behind Mashrafe Mortaza (7);<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=4493;type=series |title=Records / New Zealand in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2008/09 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> however Shakib scored just 16 runs in the series.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=4493;type=series |title=Records / New Zealand in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2008/09 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref>

The following month, Bangladesh toured [[Bangladeshi cricket team in South Africa in 2008–09|South Africa]] for two Tests, three ODIs, and a T20I. While Bangladesh lost all their matches against South Africa except for an abandoned ODI,<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/rsavbdesh/engine/series/350336.html |title=Bangladesh tour of South Africa 2008/09 / Results |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib continued to build on the good bowling form he had found against New Zealand. On the first day of the opening Test, Shakib went wicketless; on the advice of Mohammad Salauddin, Bangladesh's assistant coach, he gave the ball [[Flight (cricket)|flight]] on the second day and went on to take five wickets. He took another five-wicket haul in the second Test, again as Bangladesh lost to South Africa.<ref name="From Magura to No. 1" /> Along with South Africa's [[Makhaya Ntini]], Shakib was the series' leading wicket-taker with 11 at an average of 20.81.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=4291;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in South Africa Test Series, 2008/09 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib's performance against South Africa in a losing cause prompted former Australian [[leg spin]] bowler [[Kerry O'Keeffe]] to describe him as the "world's best finger spinner at the moment".<ref name="From Magura to No. 1" /> Sri Lanka [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2008–09|toured Bangladesh in December 2008 and January 2009]] for two Tests and a Tri-nation tournament including Zimbabwe. Sri Lanka won both Tests and the tournament final,<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bdeshvsl/engine/series/378736.html |title=Sri Lanka tour of Bangladesh 2008/09 / Results |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> although Shakib turned in a man of the match performance, scoring 92 not out, in the second ODI against Sri Lanka helped Bangladesh to their only victory against them on the tour.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib powers Bangladesh to final |date=14 January 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/tri-nation-tournament-in-bangladesh-2008-09-378748/bangladesh-vs-sri-lanka-3rd-match-378755/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> In the first match of the Test series, Shakib took another five-wicket haul as his team again was defeated.<ref name="From Magura to No. 1" />

On 22 January 2009, Shakib was ranked first amongst ODI all-rounders by the ICC.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib takes top spot among ODI allrounders |date=22 January 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-takes-top-spot-among-odi-allrounders-387457 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref>

=== Captaincy and vice-captaincy (2009–2011) ===
[[File:Shakib al hasan 3.jpg|thumb|left|Shakib was appointed Bangladesh's vice-captain in June 2009.]]
At the beginning of 2009, there was speculation over [[Mohammad Ashraful]] and his  position as captain after a succession of defeats for Bangladesh and continuous poor form for Ashraful. Shakib was considered a possible successor by the [[Bangladesh Cricket Board]] (BCB). However, the BCB was cautious of over-burdening the all-rounder and decided against the move. Other candidates were discounted, and Ashraful remained as captain.<ref>{{citation |title=Ashraful to continue as Bangladesh captain |date=8 February 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ashraful-to-continue-as-bangladesh-captain-389739 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 March 2009}}</ref> Later in 2009, Ashraful's captaincy was again under scrutiny after Bangladesh exited the [[2009 ICC World Twenty20]] in the first round following losses to Ireland and India. When [[Mashrafe Mortaza]] replaced Mohammad Ashraful in June 2009, Shakib was appointed vice-captain, filling the position vacated by Mortaza.<ref>{{citation |title=Mashrafe named Bangladesh captain |date=23 June 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mortaza-named-bangladesh-captain-410237 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=8 July 2009}}</ref>

In July–August 2009, [[Bangladeshi cricket team in West Indies in 2009|Bangladesh toured the West Indies]]. When Mortaza injured his knee in the first Test, he was unable to take to the field on the final day and Shakib took over as captain. He and [[Mahmudullah]] led Bangladesh's bowling attack, sharing 13 wickets in the match and securing a historic win for Bangladesh.
It was Bangladesh's first against the West [[Indies]], their first overseas Test victory, and only their second Test win.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib, Mahmudullah make up for Mortaza's absence |date=13 July 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-mahmudullah-make-up-for-mortaza-s-absence-414146 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 July 2009}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/247/247186.html|title=f51408 t1923 West Indies v Bangladesh: Bangladesh in West Indies 2009 (1st Test)|work=CricketArchive|url-access=subscription|access-date=18 July 2009}}</ref> The West Indies side was very inexperienced due to the fallout of a dispute between the [[West Indies Cricket Board]] and the West Indies Players' Association over pay. The first XI had made themselves unavailable for selection and a new squad had to be chosen. Seven West Indies players made their Test debut in the match and the side was captained by [[Floyd Reifer]] who had played the last of his four Tests ten years earlier.<ref>{{citation |title=West Indies name replacement squad |date=8 July 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/west-indies-name-replacement-squad-413237 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 July 2009}}</ref> Shakib was fined 10% of his match fee for excessive appealing; bowler [[Shahadat Hossain]] was also fined and batsman [[Imrul Kayes]] was reprimanded for the same reason.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib and Shahadat fined for excessive appealing |date=14 July 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-and-shahadat-fined-for-excessive-appealing-414425 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=19 June 2009}}</ref>

==== West Indies ====
In Mortaza's absence through injury, Shakib led Bangladesh for the remainder of the tour.<ref>{{citation |last=Alter |first=Jamie |title=History beckons for Bangladesh |date=16 July 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wivbdesh2009/content/story/414664.html |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 July 2009}}</ref><ref name="step aside">{{citation |title=Mortaza happy to step aside for Shakib |date=30 July 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mortaza-happy-to-step-aside-for-shakib-416880 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 August 2009}}.</ref> Aged 22 years and 115 days at the start of the second Test, Shakib became Bangladesh's youngest captain and fifth youngest in the history of Test cricket.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/283416.html |title=Records / Test matches / Individual records (captains, players, umpires) / Youngest captains |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=23 November 2010}}</ref> Under Shakib's leadership Bangladesh went on to win the second Test, and in the process secured their first overseas series win.<ref>{{citation |last=Veera |first=Sriram |title=Raqibul and Shakib inspire first overseas series win |date=20 July 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-tour-of-west-indies-2009-380896/west-indies-vs-bangladesh-2nd-test-401072/match-report-4 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=21 July 2009}}</ref> Individually Shakib performed well, earning both the player-of-the-match and player-of-the-series awards, scoring 16 and 96 not out with the bat and taking 3/59 and 5/70 with the ball.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/wivbdesh2009/engine/current/match/401072.html|title=Scorecard: West Indies v Bangladesh, 2nd Test, 17–20 July 2009|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=21 July 2009}}</ref> He scored 159 runs in the series at an average of 53.00 and was Bangladesh's second highest run-scorer for the series;<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=5037;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in West Indies Test Series, 2009 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 August 2009}}</ref> his haul of 13 wickets at an average of 18.76 from both matches meant Shakib was the equal highest wicket-taker for the series along with West Indies fast bowler [[Kemar Roach]].<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5037;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in West Indies Test Series, 2009 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 August 2009}}</ref> After winning the Test series 2–0, Bangladesh proceeded to whitewash the ODI series, winning 3–0. The West Indies' dispute remained unsolved for the whole of Bangladesh's tour and the West Indies continued to field an inexperienced side.<ref name="step aside" /> Shakib collected two half centuries in the ODI series, averaging 45.00, and was the third highest run-scorer in the series;<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=5036;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in West Indies ODI Series, 2009 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 August 2009}}</ref> he also took 2 wickets at an average of 48.00.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5036;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in West Indies ODI Series, 2009 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 August 2009}}</ref> For his performance in the ODIs, Shakib was named the man of the series.<ref>{{citation |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Seasons/WI/2009_WI_Bangladesh_in_West_Indies_2009.html |title=Bangladesh in West Indies 2009 |work=CricketArchive |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026120022/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Seasons/WI/2009_WI_Bangladesh_in_West_Indies_2009.html |archive-date=26 October 2012 |access-date=1 August 2009}}</ref>

==== Zimbabwe ====
Shakib was appointed captain for Bangladesh's [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Zimbabwe in 2009|tour of Zimbabwe in August 2009]] as Mortaza was still injured.<ref name="step aside" /> In the second ODI of the five match series in Zimbabwe in August 2009, Shakib scored 104 off only 64 balls before being run-out – his third ODI century – to help his team to their highest score in ODIs and lead Bangladesh to a 2–0 lead in the series.<ref>{{citation |last=Veera |first=Sriram |title=Shakib scripts convincing win |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-tour-of-zimbabwe-2009-410334/zimbabwe-vs-bangladesh-2nd-odi-410338/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 August 2009}}</ref> He finished the series with 170 runs from five matches at an average of 42.50 – fifth highest run-scorer<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=5129;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in Zimbabwe ODI Series, 2009 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 September 2009}}</ref> – and 6 wickets an average of 39.66, fourth highest wicket-taker in the series.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5129;type=series |title=Records / Bangladesh in Zimbabwe ODI Series, 2009 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 September 2009}}</ref> Following his team's 4–1 victory in the ODI series against Zimbabwe, Shakib travelled to Australia to undergo medical treatment for acute groin pain. He had been experiencing pain since the end of the West Indies tour, but he had decided to play through the pain and lead Bangladesh in Zimbabwe.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib to undergo treatment in Australia |date=27 August 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-to-undergo-treatment-in-australia-422343 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 September 2009}}</ref> Although he did not win, Shakib was nominated Cricketer of the Year and Test Player of the Year in the 2009 [[ICC Awards]]; he was the only Bangladesh player to be nominated in either category that year.<ref>{{citation |title=Dhoni, Dilshan pick up maximum nominations |date=2 September 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/dhoni-dilshan-pick-up-maximum-nominations-422973 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 September 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|url=http://icc-cricket.yahoo.net/events_and_awards/lg_icc_awards/newsdetails.php?newsId=1310_1254417540 |title=Mitchell Johnson takes top honours at glittering ICC Awards night |date=2 October 2009 |publisher=International Cricket Council |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807055221/http://icc-cricket.yahoo.net/events_and_awards/lg_icc_awards/newsdetails.php?newsId=1310_1254417540 |archive-date=7 August 2011 |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref>

Shakib's success meant that it was not a given that Mortaza would replace him as captain once fit,<ref name="step aside" /> but it was announced in September 2009 that Mortaza would return as captain for Bangladesh's home [[Zimbabwe cricket team in Bangladesh in 2009|ODI series against Zimbabwe the following month]] and Shakib would return to the role of vice-captain.<ref>{{citation |title=Mortaza appointed captain for Zimbabwe series |date=9 September 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mortaza-appointed-captain-for-zimbabwe-series-424272 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 September 2009}}</ref> However, Mortaza failed to return from arthroscopic surgery on both knees in time for the series, and Shakib was again named captain.<ref>{{citation |title=Injured Mortaza out of Zimbabwe ODIs |date=22 October 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/injured-mortaza-to-miss-zimbabwe-odis-430712 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 November 2009}}</ref> After losing the opening match – in which Shakib criticised the performance of Bangladesh's batsmen including himself<ref>{{citation |title=We can still win this 4–1 – Shakib |date=27 October 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/we-can-still-win-this-4-1-shakib-431572 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 November 2009}}</ref> – Bangladesh went on to win the series 4–1.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bdeshvzim09/engine/series/422622.html |title=Zimbabwe tour of Bangladesh 2009/10 / Results |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> In the second match of the series, Shakib passed 2,000 runs in ODIs.<ref name="ODI cumulative batting average" />

On 5 November 2009, Shakib became no. 1 ODI bowler in ICC rankings.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.relianceiccrankings.com/datespecific/odi/bowling/2009/11/05/|title=ICC ODI Championship Bowling Rankings-Date Specific Rankings-05/11/2009|work=Reliance ICC Rankings|date=5 November 2009|access-date=1 July 2021}}</ref>

In November 2009, Shakib was named ''[[The Wisden Cricketer]]'s'' "Test Player of the Year".<ref name="Test player of the year">{{citation |url=http://wisdencricketer.com/item.php?parent_id=3&child_id=0&item_id=599 |title=Remember The Name |work=The Wisden Cricketer online |first=Rabeed |last=Imam |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091012075533/http://wisdencricketer.com/item.php?parent_id=3&child_id=0&item_id=599 |archive-date=12 October 2009 |access-date=11 October 2009}}</ref>

==== England and the Asia Cup ====
[[File:Shakib al hasan 4.jpg|thumb|upright|Shakib in the field against England during the second ODI, shortly after relinquishing the captaincy]]
Over February and March 2010 [[English cricket team in Bangladesh in 2009–10|England toured Bangladesh]] for two Tests and three ODIs. England won all of their matches against Bangladesh.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/bdeshveng2010/engine/series/426373.html |title=England tour of Bangladesh 2009/10 / Results |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib was Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker in both the Test and ODI series (9 in Tests and 5 in ODIs).<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5510;type=series |title=Records / England in Bangladesh Test Series, 2009/10 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref><ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5509;type=series |title=Records / England in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2009/10 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Both Tests went to the final day and Shakib expressed the opinion that the experience had exhausted his side.<ref>{{citation |last=Miller |first=Andrew |title=Bangladesh ran out of steam – Shakib |date=24 March 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-al-hasan-admits-bangladesh-ran-out-of-steam-453368 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> The match was also a source of controversy after incorrect umpiring decisions on the third day went against Bangladesh, prompting Shakib to blame the lack of a [[Umpire Decision Review System|referral system]] for some of the team's misfortune.<ref>{{citation |last=Miller |first=Andrew |title=Shakib blames board for lack of review system |date=22 March 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-blames-board-for-lack-of-review-system-453049 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> In turn, Bangladesh [[Bangladeshi cricket team in England in 2010|toured England in May and July]] the same year. They again lost the Test series 2–0.<ref name="England 2010 results">{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/england-v-bangladesh-2010/engine/series/426339.html |title=Bangladesh tour of England, Ireland and Scotland 2010 / Results |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Shakib finished as his team's leading wicket-taker with eight wickets,<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/england-v-bangladesh-2010/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5504;type=series |title=Bangladesh in England Test Series, 2010 / Records / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> although he only scored 52 runs.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/england-v-bangladesh-2010/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=5504;type=series |title=Bangladesh in England Test Series, 2010 / Records / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Before the ODI series, Bangladesh left England for Sri Lanka, which was hosting the [[2010 Asia Cup]] in June. Bangladesh lost all three of their matches.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/asia2010/engine/series/424694.html |title=Asia Cup 2010 / Results |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> With five wickets, Shakib was Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker with [[Shafiul Islam]] (5 each).<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/asia2010/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5477;type=tournament |title=Asia Cup, 2010 / Records / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref>

As he was struggling to cope with the captaincy and his role as an all-rounder, Shakib gave up the captaincy in July 2010 to focus on his own performance. Mashrafe Mortaza returned to take charge in ODIs. Coach Jamie Siddons explained that "Shakib was the main person behind the decision, he decided it was a bit much for him. His form was down with the bat and he needed a rest."<ref>{{citation |last=McGlashan |first=Andrew |title=Shakib is an ideal captain – Siddons |date=5 July 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-in-england-siddons-sees-captaincy-future-for-shakib-466199 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> Bangladesh returned to England for the ODI half of their tour. Bangladesh lost the series 2–1,<ref name="England 2010 results" /> but their victory in the second match was the first time Bangladesh had beaten England in international cricket.<ref>{{citation |last=McGlashan |first=Andrew |title=Bangladesh seal historic victory |date=10 July 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-tour-of-england-ireland-and-scotland-2010-426339/england-vs-bangladesh-2nd-odi-426404/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> While in Europe, Bangladesh were scheduled to play two ODIs against Ireland, and one each against Scotland and Netherlands. The match against Scotland was abandoned and Bangladesh lost one match to each of Ireland and the Netherlands.<ref name="England 2010 results" />

For his performances in 2009, he was named in the World Test XI by the ICC.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/johnson-and-gambhir-scoop-top-awards-427665|title=Johnson and Gambhir scoop top awards|website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

==== New Zealand and Zimbabwe ====
In October 2010, [[New Zealand cricket team in Bangladesh in 2010–11|New Zealand went to Bangladesh]] for five ODIs. In the first match of the series Mortaza injured his ankle and was forced to leave the field; Shakib took over, and under his leadership Bangladesh secured a nine-run victory, during which Shakib took four wickets and scored 58. Once it emerged that Mortaza would be unable to play in the rest of the series, Shakib was made captain for the remaining matches.<ref>{{citation |title=Mortaza ruled out due to injury |date=6 October 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/new-zealand-in-bangladesh-2010-mashrafe-mortaza-ruled-out-due-to-injury-480285 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> In the fourth match, Shakib scored a century and took three wickets to help his team win by nine runs.<ref name="NZ 4th ODI 2010">{{citation |last=Fernando |first=Andrew |title=All-round Shakib inspires Bangladesh to historic win |date=14 October 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-tour-of-bangladesh-2010-11-476044/bangladesh-vs-new-zealand-4th-odi-476599/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> Bangladesh went on to win the series 4–0,<ref>{{citation |last=Isam |first=Mohammad |title=Bangladesh reap rewards of hard work |date=18 October 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/new-zealand-in-bangladesh-2010-bangladesh-reap-rewards-of-hard-work-482305 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> their first series victory against a full strength ICC Full Member nation.<ref name="NZ 4th ODI 2010" /> Shakib finished the series as the player with most runs and wickets on either side: 213 runs<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6168;type=series |title=Records / New Zealand in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2010/11 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref> and 11 wickets.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=6168;type=series |title=Records / New Zealand in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2010/11 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 November 2010}}</ref>

Although Mortaza returned from injury in time for Zimbabwe's tour of Bangladesh in December, Shakib was retained as captain for the five-match ODI series.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib retained as captain for Zimbabwe series |date=28 November 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/zimbabwe-in-bangladesh-shakib-retained-as-captain-for-zimbabwe-series-489535 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=29 November 2010}}</ref> Following his side's defeat in the opening ODI, Shakib stated that he "was not prepared to take the job and I am also not satisfied with my role as a captain".<ref>{{citation |title='I was not prepared for captaincy' – Shakib Al Hasan |date=2 December 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-v-zimbabwe-i-was-not-prepared-for-captaincy-shakib-al-hasan-490108 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=2 December 2010}}</ref> Bangladesh went on to win the next three complete matches, with one called off due to rain, to beat Zimbabwe 3–1.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib praises Bangladesh recovery |date=12 December 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-v-zimbabwe-shakib-praises-bangladesh-recovery-491571 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=12 December 2010}}</ref> Shakib was Bangladesh's second-highest run-scorer and wicket taker for the series with 156 runs, including two half centuries, and nine wickets.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6321;type=series |title=Records / Zimbabwe in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2010/11 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=12 December 2010}}</ref><ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=6321;type=series |title=Records / Zimbabwe in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2010/11 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=12 December 2010}}</ref>

==== 2011 World Cup ====

In February to March April 2011, Bangladesh co-hosted the [[2011 Cricket World Cup|World Cup]] with India and Sri Lanka. West Indies dismissed Bangladesh for 58 runs, the team's lowest score in ODIs and a record low for a Full Member at the World Cup.<ref>{{citation |last=Monga |first=Sidharth |title=Bangladesh are devastated - Siddons |date=6 March 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/world-cup-2011-bangladesh-are-devastated-jamie-siddons-504517 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 March 2011}}</ref> Shakib described this match as the 'worst day' of his career.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.outlookindia.com/newswire/story/worst-day-of-my-career-bangladesh-captain/713878|title=Worst Day of My Career: Bangladesh Captain|work=Outlook India|date=4 March 2011|access-date=7 June 2021}}</ref> Shakib's house was stoned by angry fans in the aftermath,<ref>{{citation |last=Monga |first=Sidharth |title=Shakib, Siddons hit back at criticism from former players |date=6 March 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/world-cup-2011-bangladesh-captain-and-coach-hit-back-at-criticism-from-former-players-504533 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 March 2011}}</ref> as was the West Indies team bus as it left the ground.<ref>{{citation |last=Monga |first=Sidharth |title=West Indies team bus stoned in Dhaka |date=4 March 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-v-west-indies-west-indies-team-bus-stoned-in-dhaka-504279 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 March 2011}}</ref> Bangladesh registered wins against England, Ireland and the Netherlands, but defeats by West Indies, India and South Africa meant they did not progress beyond the first round of the tournament.<ref>{{citation |last=Purohit |first=Abhishek |title=Abject Bangladesh surrender meekly |date=19 March 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2010-11-381449/bangladesh-vs-south-africa-39th-match-group-b-433597/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 March 2011}}</ref> With 8 wickets at an average of 27.87, Shakib was Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker in the tournament,<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/icc_cricket_worldcup2011/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=4857;type=tournament |title=ICC Cricket World Cup, 2010/11 / Records / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 March 2011}}</ref> and his 142 runs from 6 innings made him the team's third highest run-scorer.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/icc_cricket_worldcup2011/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=4857;type=tournament |title=ICC Cricket World Cup, 2010/11 / Records / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 March 2011}}</ref>

=== After World Cup ===
Shortly after the World Cup, [[Australian cricket team in Bangladesh in 2011|Australia toured Bangladesh]] for three ODIs. In the first match of the series, Shakib scored 51 to pass 3,000 runs in ODIs.<ref name="ODI cumulative batting average" /> Bangladesh lost the series 3–0,<ref>{{citation |last=Coverdale |first=Brydon |title=Hussey hundred sets up Australia's clean-sweep |date=13 April 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-tour-of-bangladesh-2011-503357/bangladesh-vs-australia-3rd-odi-503365/match-report |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 April 2011}}</ref> Shakib scored 69 runs in three matches<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6486;type=series |title=Records / Australia in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2011 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 April 2011}}</ref> and took just one wicket whilst conceding 117 runs.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=6486;type=series |title=Records / Australia in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2011 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 April 2011}}</ref> [[Shane Watson]]'s performances in the series meant he was ranked first amongst ODI all-rounders, claiming the position from Shakib.<ref>{{citation |title=Watson rises to top spot in ICC rankings |date=15 April 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/icc-rankings-shane-watson-rises-top-spot-in-icc-rankings-511114 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 April 2011}}</ref>

When Bangladesh toured Zimbabwe in [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Zimbabwe in 2011|August 2011]] they were expected to win the one-off Test, which was Zimbabwe's first in five years, and the five-match ODI series. As it transpired Bangladesh lost the ODI series 3–2 and the Test. Shakib and his vice-captain, Tamim Iqbal, were sacked with a BCB official citing unsatisfactory leadership.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib and Tamim stripped of leadership roles |date=5 September 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-news-shakib-and-tamim-stripped-of-leadership-roles-531274 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=5 September 2011}}</ref>

=== Post-captaincy (2011–2017) ===
Bangladesh's first series under new leadership was [[West Indian cricket team in Bangladesh in 2011–12|against the West Indies in October 2011]]. Relieved of the captaincy, Shakib was Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker in both the ODI and Test series,<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=6863;type=series |title=Records / West Indies in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2011/12 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=6864;type=series |title=Records / West Indies in Bangladesh Test Series, 2011/12 / Most wickets |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref> his bowling was backed up by 168 runs in the two Tests (of the Bangladesh players, only Tamim Iqbal scored more),<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6864;type=series |title=Records / West Indies in Bangladesh Test Series, 2011/12 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref> and 79 from two innings in the ODIs.<ref>{{citation |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6863;type=series |title=Records / West Indies in Bangladesh ODI Series, 2011/12 / Most runs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref> Bangladesh lost both series.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/series/531420.html |title=West Indies tour of Bangladesh 2011/12 / Results |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref> Following this, Shakib was Bangladesh's top run-scorer and wicket-taker in the [[Pakistani cricket team in Bangladesh in 2011–12|home Test series]] against Pakistan in December 2011.<ref>{{citation|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=6957;type=series|title=Pakistan in Bangladesh Test Series, 2011/12: Most wickets|publisher=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6957;type=series|title=Pakistan in Bangladesh Test Series, 2011/12: Most runs|publisher=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref> In the second Test of the series, he became Bangladesh's first player to score a century (his highest score, 144) and take five wickets in an innings in the same Test.<ref>{{citation |last=Ravindran |first=Siddarth |title=Pakistan in charge despite Shakib's six-for |date=20 December 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-tour-of-bangladesh-2011-12-538064/bangladesh-vs-pakistan-2nd-test-538073/match-report-4 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=21 December 2011}}</ref> After the series he moved to first place in the ICC's ranking of Test all-rounders.<ref>{{citation |title=Shakib becomes No. 1 Test allrounder |date=22 December 2011 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/icc-rankings-shakib-al-hasan-becomes-no-1-test-allrounder-546592 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=27 December 2011}}</ref>

In the [[West Indian cricket team in Bangladesh in 2012–13|home series against West Indies in late 2012]], he became the 2nd Bangladeshi to both take 100 Test wickets, making him the leading wicket-taker in Tests for Bangladesh, and to complete the 1000 run / 100 wicket double.<ref>{{citation |last=Balachandran |first=Kanishkaa |title=A high and low for Shakib Al Hasan |date=24 November 2012 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/a-high-and-low-for-shakib-al-hasan-592795 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 December 2012}}</ref> However, he got ruled out of the ODI and T20 series due to a shin injury.<ref>{{citation |last=Isam |first=Mohammad |title=Shakib out of rest of West Indies ODIs |date=1 December 2012 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-al-hasan-out-of-rest-of-west-indies-odis-594591 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 December 2012}}</ref>

Shakib got ruled out of the [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2012–13|Sri Lanka tour]] in March due to a calf muscle injury. He had a successful operation on the right leg at a private hospital in [[Sydney]], [[Australia]]. He would be on rest for one month since his operation.<ref>{{citation |url=http://bdnews24.com/cricket/2013/02/26/shakibs-surgery-successful |title=Shakib's surgery successful |first=Mohammad |last=Isam |work=bdnews24.com |date=26 February 2013 |access-date=27 February 2013}}</ref>

In 2nd Test match of [[Zimbabwean cricket team in Bangladesh in 2014–15|Zimbabwe tour of Bangladesh 2014]] Shakib became only the fourth player in Test history after [[Alan Davidson (cricketer, born 1929)|Alan Davidson]] (1960), [[Ian Botham]] (1980) and [[Imran Khan]] (1983) to score a hundred and take 10 wickets in the same match.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alan Davidson, star of tied 1960 Test, dies at 92|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/alan-davidson-star-of-tied-1960-test-dies-at-92-1286036|access-date=3 November 2021|website=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>

On 7 December 2014, Shakib became no. 1 T20 all-rounder.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.daily-sun.com/post/19143/Shakib-Salma-ranked-No.-1-T20-allrounder|title=Shakib, Salma ranked No. 1 T-20 all-rounder|work=[[Daily Sun]]|date=7 December 2014|access-date=7 June 2021}}</ref>

In 2015, Shakib helped Bangladesh to their most successful year in cricket. Following their success in the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]] (where after batting in the first match at [[2015 Cricket World Cup]], he had a total of 4,040 runs in ODI matches and became the first Bangladeshi cricketer to score 4,000 runs in ODIs),<ref name="auto1">{{cite news | url=http://bdnews24.com/cricket/2015/02/18/shakib-al-hasan-first-bangladesh-player-to-score-4000-odi-runs | title=Shakib Al Hasan first Bangladesh player to score 4,000 ODI runs | work=[[Bdnews24.com]] | date=18 February 2015 | access-date=18 February 2015}}</ref> he also helped the team to a whitewash of Pakistan and series win against India and South Africa. On 12 June, he captured his 100th Test wicket at home on the third day of the one-off Test match against India.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/shakib-al-hasan-completes-100-test-wickets-bangladesh-vs-india-257222-2015-06-12|title=Bangladesh star Shakib Al Hasan completes 100 Test wickets at home|work=[[India Today]]|date=12 June 2015|access-date=19 May 2021}}</ref> On 15 July, he took his 200th wicket of his ODI career by taking the wicket of [[Hashim Amla]] in the final ODI of the ODI series becoming the fastest, youngest and the only seventh cricketer to 4,000 runs and 200 wickets double in ODIs (in 156 matches).{{efn|other cricketers are [[Sanath Jayasuriya]] (235 matches), [[Shahid Afridi]] (238 matches), [[Jacques Kallis]] (221 matches), [[Abdul Razzaq]] (204 matches), [[Chris Harris (cricketer)|Chris Harris]] (244 matches) and [[Chris Cairns]] (213 matches)}}<ref name="200wickets">{{cite news|url =https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/cricket/shakib-takes-200-odi-wickets-112939|title=Shakib takes 200 ODI wickets|work=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]]|date=15 July 2015|access-date=29 March 2021}}</ref><ref name="4000runs">{{cite news|url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/cricket/stats-shakib-al-hasan-quickest-complete-double-of-4000-runs-200-wickets-odis|title=Stats: Shakib Al Hasan – Quickest to complete double of 4000 runs and 200 wickets in ODIs|work=Sportskeeda|date=19 July 2015|access-date=29 March 2021}}</ref>

On 26 September 2016, with the wicket of [[Shabir Noori]] during the first ODI against Afghanistan, Shakib became Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker in ODIs as well as in all formats at that time.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/cricket/bangladesh-vs-afghanistan-2016/shakib-al-hasan-bangladeshs-global-ambassador-1289965?amp|title=Shakib Al Hasan: Bangladesh's global ambassador|work=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]]|date=26 September 2016|access-date=19 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.daily-sun.com/post/169984/Shakib-Al-Hasan:-The-pioneer-of-Bangladesh-cricket|title=Shakib Al Hasan: The pioneer of Bangladesh cricket|work=[[Daily Sun]]|date=26 September 2016|access-date=19 May 2021}}</ref>

On 22 October 2016, with the wicket of [[Joe Root]], Shakib became the first Bangladeshi to have bagged 150 Test scalps.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://en.prothomalo.com/amp/story/sports/Shakib-double-stings-England|title=Shakib double stings England|work=[[Prothom Alo]]|date=22 October 2016|access-date=19 May 2021}}</ref>

=== New era of Test & T20I captaincy (2017–2019) ===
After the retirement from T20I of [[Mashrafe Mortaza]] in 2017, Shakib was appointed as the T20I captain of the team for the second time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cricketcountry.com/news/shakib-al-hasan-appointed-bangladeshs-t20i-captain-598395 |title=Shakib Al Hasan appointed Bangladesh's T20I captain |publisher=Cricket Country |access-date=22 April 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/sports/shakib-officially-t20-captain-1394791 |title=Shakib officially T20 captain |work=The Daily Star |access-date=22 April 2017}}</ref> Later [[Mushfiqur Rahim]] was also removed from Test captaincy and Hasan was again appointed as Test captain.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shakib-al-hasan-named-new-bangladesh-test-captain-1129104|title=Shakib named new Bangladesh Test captain|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|date=10 December 2017|access-date=21 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.india.com/sports/shakib-al-hasan-appointed-as-bangladesh-test-captain-2736047/|title=Shakib Al Hasan Appointed as Bangladesh Test Captain|website=India.com|date=10 December 2017|access-date=21 May 2021}}</ref> However, during [[2017–18 Bangladesh Tri-Nation Series]], he injured his finger and was rested for few days. In his absence, [[Mahmudullah]] captained the side in the [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2017–18|Home series against Sri Lanka]] and [[2018 Nidahas Trophy]]. His first tour was against [[Pakistani cricket team in Bangladesh in 2017|Pakistan in July 2017.]]

On 28 August 2017, Al Hasan became the 4th bowler in Test history to record a 5-wicket haul against all Test Playing nations (except Afghanistan and Ireland, who have only just granted Test status earlier that year) when he grabbed 5 wickets against Australia in his first encounter with the team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cricketcountry.com/news/shakib-al-hasan-joins-exclusive-list-takes-five-wicket-hauls-against-all-nations-637312|title=Shakib Al Hasan joins an exclusive list, takes five-wicket hauls against all nations|work= Cricket Country|date=28 August 2017|access-date=17 December 2020}}</ref> He also scored a half-century in the first innings. In the second innings, he only scored 8 runs with the bat, but he grabbed another 5 wickets to secure his first [[10-wicket haul]] and the win.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cricket.com.au/news/shakib-al-hasan-five-wicket-haul-bangladesh-australia-every-test-playing-nation-herath-murali-steyn/2017-08-28|title=Shakib joins legends with record five|work=cricket.com.au|access-date=28 August 2017|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://live.cricket.com.au/#/2032/41972|title=Live & Official Cricket Scores {{!}} cricket.com.au|website=live.cricket.com.au|access-date=30 August 2017}}</ref> However, after the series, Al Hasan opted to take a break from Test to focus on limited-overs games.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/shakib-al-hasan-bangladesh-vs-australia-test-cricket-south-africa-vs-bangladesh-1043165-2017-09-12|title=Shakib Al Hasan's six months break could derail Bangladesh's Test push ahead of busy season|work=[[India Today]]|date=12 September 2017|access-date=17 December 2020}}</ref>

In April 2018, he was one of ten cricketers to be awarded a central contract by the [[Bangladesh Cricket Board]] (BCB) ahead of the 2018 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=BCB cuts contracts list for 2018 to ten |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bcb-cuts-contracts-list-for-2018-to-ten-1143673 |access-date=18 April 2018 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Later the same month, he was named in the [[World XI (cricket)|Rest of the World XI]] squad for the [[West Indies v ICC World XI in England in 2018|one-off T20I]] against the [[West Indies national cricket team|West Indies]], played at [[Lord's]] on 31 May 2018,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/670194 |title=Rashid, Tamim and Shakib confirmed for ICC World XI team to play the Windies at Lord's |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=23 April 2018}}</ref> but later withdrew from squad due to personal reason.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/691274|title=Sandeep Lamichhane added to the ICC World XI for 31 May T20I against the Windies at Lord's|access-date=16 May 2018|work=International Cricket Council}}</ref>

In November 2018, in the series [[West Indian cricket team in Bangladesh in 2018–19|against the West Indies]], he became the first bowler for Bangladesh to [[List of Bangladesh Test cricket records#Most ducks|take 200 wickets in Tests]].<ref name="SAH200" /> In the same match, he also became the fastest cricketer, in terms of matches, to score 3,000 runs and take 200 wickets in Tests, doing so in his 54th match.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/bangladesh-cricket/news/shakib-becomes-fastest-200-wicket-3000-run-double-1664536 |title=Shakib becomes fastest to 200-wicket, 3,000-run double |work=The Daily Star |access-date=24 November 2018}}</ref>

===2023 onwards=== 
In the 2nd ODI [[English cricket team in Bangladesh in 2022-23|against England]] Shakib scored 58 runs from 69 balls while chasing a tough target of 327 runs set by England. He was the standing captain in the first test [[Bangladeshi cricket team in the West Indies in 2009|against West Indies in 2009]], when regular captain [[Mashrafe Mortaza]] left the field on the first day due injury. Bangladesh went on to win the test match which was the first away test win for Bangladesh. He also captained the team for the second test as well and leading the team to win the match and consequently winning the series, which was their first away test series win also. He was named Player of the series for his all-round performance.

He captained Bangladesh against [[West Indian cricket team in Bangladesh in 2018–19|West Indies in 2018–19]], when Bangladesh defeated them 2–0, which was their second test series win against them. He was named Player of the Series for his all-round performances. During his stint as test captain, Bangladesh won only these 3 tests out of  14 matches.

Bangladesh played 50 ODI matches under his captaincy from 2009 to 2015 and won 23 matches. He was also the Bangladesh captain in [[2011 Cricket World Cup]] and also captained 1 match in [[2015 Cricket World Cup]].

Bangladesh also played 34 T20I matches under his captaincy, winning 12 matches.

He captained Bangladesh against [[English cricket team in Bangladesh in 2022-23|England in 2022–23]], when Bangladesh defeated them 3–0, which was their first T20I series win against them.

* Second Bangladeshi batsmen to score 10,000 international runs.{{efn|First is [[Tamim Iqbal]].}}<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thefinancialexpress.com.bd/sports/tamim-reaches-landmark-of-odi-11000-run-shakib-10000-1516379813|title=Tamim reaches landmark of 11000 run,Shakib 10000|work=[[The Financial Express (Bangladesh)|The Financial Express]]|access-date=21 October 2020}}</ref>
* Second highest individual score (217) by a Bangladeshi batsman in Tests.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_innings.html?class=1;id=25;type=team|title=Records / Bangladesh / Test Matches / High Scores|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=29 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=12 January 2017 |title=Bangladesh 542, Shakib 217, Mushfiqur 159 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-tour-of-new-zealand-2016-17-1019965/new-zealand-vs-bangladesh-1st-test-1019985/match-report-2 |access-date=25 September 2017 |publisher=[[ESPNcricinfo]]}}</ref>{{efn|Highest one is by [[Mushfiqur Rahim]] who scored 219* [[Zimbabwean cricket team in Bangladesh in 2018–19|against Zimbabwe in 2018]].}}
* Third-highest run-scorer for Bangladesh in all formats (12,070 runs) as of 18 July 2021.{{efn|behind [[Tamim Iqbal]] (14023) and [[Mushfiqur Rahim]] (12599).}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?class=11;id=25;type=team|title=Records / Bangladesh / Combined Test, ODI, and T20I Records / Most Runs|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref>
* On 18 March 2022, in the 1st ODI [[Bangladeshi cricket team in South Africa in 2021–22#1st ODI|against South Africa]], he scored his fiftieth half-centuries in [[One Day International|ODIs]], being only 2nd Bangladeshi batsman to do so after [[Tamim Iqbal]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=হাসান |first1=মেহেদী |title=ক্যালিস–জয়াসুরিয়ার পাশে সাকিব ছাড়া আর কেউ নেই |url=https://www.prothomalo.com/sports/cricket/%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%9C%E0%A7%9F%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A7%9F%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%AC-%E0%A6%9B%E0%A6%BE%E0%A7%9C%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%89-%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%87 |access-date=19 March 2022 |work=Prothomalo |language=bn}}</ref>
